newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Irish minister sees way to ease British beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Irish minister sees way to ease British beef ban.

text.p: Irish Farm Minister Ivan Yates said on Wednesday that one way of ending an impasse over easing a British beef export ban would be to carry out a selective cull, with perhaps a certified herd scheme for Northern Ireland.
He said the Irish EU presidency had contacted other member states to estimate support for such a proposal, which would have to come from Britain.

"The majority of states were sympathetic to something that would limit animal movements between Northern Ireland and the rest of United Kingdom," Yates told a news conference after a three-day meeting of EU farm ministers.

The EU imposed a global ban on British beef exports in March after the British government said it was possible that the fatal cattle brain disease bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) could be passed to people who ate infected beef.

Yates stressed the need to respect an agreement by EU leaders in Florence for a gradual lifting of the ban subject to fulfilment of strict conditions to eradicate BSE, including a selective slaughter of cattle most at risk.
The agreement set out a clear procedure, the first step being for Britain to put forward a working document on a region of Britain or Northern Ireland, he added.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said EU scientists must give their support before the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of senior national officials could take a decision. "The first move has to be made by the British government," he said.
